message.content: I'm sorry you're feeling unwell. Let me ask a few focused questions. Have you had any fever, chills, chest pain, or coughed up any blood? Also, have you had any leg swelling or pain, recent travel or surgery, and do you have any known heart or lung conditions or take any regular medications?

Thanks, doctor. For the past week I've been short of breath and I have a new dry cough, nothing coming up. I wasn't told about fever, chills, chest pain, coughing blood, leg swelling, or recent travel or surgery, so I can't say I've had any of those. As for my health, I have rheumatoid arthritis, and I've had a lung condition called interstitial lung disease from it for about five years. It's been stable. I also was around asbestos material at some point. I take baricitinib and methotrexate for the arthritis, and I've been on the same doses for a while. I'm not sure about my other medicines or allergies right now.

Thank you for the details. You have rheumatoid arthritis with long-standing lung scarring (interstitial lung disease), and you take methotrexate and baricitinib. Both drugs weaken the immune system, and methotrexate can also irritate the lungs. That makes several causes possible: an infection such as Pneumocystis pneumonia, a flare of the lung scarring, a drug reaction in the lungs, or a blood clot. Baricitinib raises clot risk. Your past asbestos exposure also matters. I'll start with a physical exam, including your oxygen level, breathing rate, heart and lung sounds, and any leg swelling. After that I'll decide which tests to order.

This could be an infection such as Pneumocystis pneumonia. It could also be a flare of your lung scarring, a reaction to a medicine, or fluid or a growth around the lung related to asbestos. Next I'll order a chest CT scan, a chest X-ray, blood tests (blood count, kidney and liver tests, inflammation markers, LDH, beta-D-glucan and BNP), and an arterial blood gas. I'll also order a respiratory infection panel, including Pneumocystis PCR. These tests should show which of these causes is most likely.

message.content: Your CT scan shows fluid around the left lung and nodular thickening of the lining of the lung (the pleura), including the part next to the center of the chest. With your past asbestos exposure, this raises concern for a pleural tumor such as mesothelioma. Infection and a flare of your lung scarring are less likely to explain these findings, because your inflammatory markers are not high. To confirm, I'm ordering analysis and cytology of the pleural fluid and a biopsy of the pleura with special tissue stains.

message.content: Your pleural fluid and biopsy results show cells that stain for SOX10, Melan-A and S100. These are melanoma markers. The cells did not stain for the markers of mesothelioma (calretinin, WT1), so this is not mesothelioma despite your asbestos exposure. The most likely diagnosis is metastatic melanoma in the lining of the left lung, with fluid around the lung. No skin or eye lesion was found on examination, so the original site is unknown. The infection and the lung-scarring flare I was worried about earlier are much less likely. The next steps are a PET-CT scan, a brain MRI, and BRAF mutation testing. You should also see oncology, and your arthritis medicines (baricitinib and methotrexate) should be reviewed. Draining the fluid can help your breathing in the meantime.
